answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks from independently trusted seeds, so voting weight reflects reachable, supported paths rather than claimed identities. A sybil cluster isolated behind a sparse external cut has low conductance—the cut’s edge weight is small relative to the cluster’s volume—and receives little walk mass across that boundary. Like a canyon, reef, or jetty separating channels, this bottleneck limits aggregate influence, provided edge weights and seed trust are authenticated.
